info.name: Polkurier API
info.description:
Every API method the Polkurier PHP SDK sends, as raw requests, with each response shape and the errors a caller can run into.

## Layout

- One folder per SDK service: `Orders` is `$client->orders()`.
- Inside it, one folder per API method, named by its `apimethod` value.
- Inside that, one request per variant: a success request for every response shape (a parameter that changes the response gets its own request) and the errors a caller can run into. `Common errors` holds the errors any method can return.

Every request has a saved example response, recorded on the sandbox.

## Setup

1. Import this collection and the `Polkurier sandbox` environment.
2. In the environment, set `login` (your account number) and `token` (your API token).
3. `baseUrl` points at the sandbox. Change it to `https://api.polkurier.pl` for production.

## How the API works

Every call is a `POST /` with a JSON body: `apimethod` names the method, `authorization` carries the credentials and `data` holds the method's parameters. The API answers HTTP 200 even for errors, so read the body's `status`: `success` comes with `response`, `error` with a message in `response` and, when present, `status_code` and `error_code`.

## Running it

Each request's tests check `status` and, for an error, its codes. Requests that create a record save its identifier in a collection variable that later requests in the same service use, so run a service's folder top to bottom, e.g. in the Collection Runner. A pre-request script fills `{{today}}`, `{{nextWorkday}}`, `{{nextSunday}}`, `{{weekAgo}}`, `{{monthAgo}}` and `{{randomSuffix}}`.

Folders marked **Changes data** create, change or delete records on the account; they remove what they create where the API allows it.

## Manual requests

Manual requests need data or codes you supply (a two-factor code, a valid coupon, an invoice on the account), or change something the collection can't put back, such as the password. They are skipped unless the environment's `runManualRequests` variable is `true`. Their example responses are illustrative, not recorded. Set `twoFactorToken` and `twoFactorCode` in the collection variables before sending a request that needs a two-factor confirmation.

item.name: Common errors
item.description: Errors any method can return because of the request envelope or the credentials. The SDK throws `AuthorizationException` for the credential errors and `WebserviceException` for the rest.

request.description: A method that needs credentials, sent without the `authorization` object.
An unknown login gets the same answer.
The message repeats the value in brackets.
The same error as an unknown `apimethod`, with empty brackets.
Any HTTP method other than POST gets this error, still with HTTP 200.

item.name: Utils
item.description: Connectivity and credential checks. `$client->utils()`.

item.name: heartbeat
item.description: Confirms the API is reachable and reports its clock. Needs no credentials, so the request has no `authorization` block. `$client->utils()->heartbeat()`.

request.description: The request has no `data` either. `time` is the server's clock in ISO 8601; compare it with yours to catch clock skew.

item.name: test_auth_api
item.description: Verifies a set of credentials and does nothing else, e.g. a token a customer has just pasted in. `$client->utils()->testAuthApi()` takes them as an argument instead of using the configured ones.

request.description: `authorization` is always true: bad credentials get an authorization error instead (see Common errors).

item.name: System
item.description: Service limits, carrier notices and coupon checks. `$client->system()`.

item.name: get_system_info
item.description: Returns the service limits to validate input against: security PIN lengths, the two-factor code length and resend window, attachment limits, the minimum coupon length, the bank verification transfer amount and the period for accepting revised terms. `$client->system()->getSystemInfo()`.

request.description: The values can change without an API version bump. The response has no account data, so it can be cached across a process.

item.name: get_couriers_messages
item.description: Returns current carrier notices (delays, suspensions, general information) to show before a customer picks a carrier. Pass `courier` for one carrier's notices only. `$client->system()->getCouriersMessages()`.

request.description: Each notice names the carrier and has a `type` (`ALERT`: orders placed now are affected; `MESSAGE`: informational) and a display `severity`. The text is Polish HTML, ready to display. With nothing to report the response is `[]`.

item.name: validate_coupon_code
item.description: Checks a discount coupon, optionally against an order (carrier, shipment type and parcels). `$client->system()->validateCouponCode()`.

request.description: `valid` is false, every descriptive field and `couriers` are null, and `description` is empty.

response.name: Success: unknown code
response.body:
{
    "status": "success",
    "response": {
        "code": "NOPE123",
        "valid": false,
        "valid_for_order": false,
        "type": null,
        "value": null,
        "value_used": null,
        "usage_type": null,
        "couriers": null,
        "valid_to": null,
        "description": ""
    }
}

request.description: `valid_for_order` checks the coupon against the order's carrier, shipment type and parcels. Without them it is always false, meaning "not checked".

response.name: Success: checked against an order
response.body:
{
    "status": "success",
    "response": {
        "code": "SPRING10",
        "valid": false,
        "valid_for_order": false,
        "type": null,
        "value": null,
        "value_used": null,
        "usage_type": null,
        "couriers": null,
        "valid_to": null,
        "description": ""
    }
}

request.description:
`valid` is true; `type`, `value` and `usage_type` describe the discount, `couriers` the carriers it is limited to and `valid_to` its expiry. Place the order with the returned `code`, which may differ from the one sent.

*Manual request: skipped unless the `runManualRequests` variable is `true`. It needs data or codes you supply, or it changes things the collection can't put back. Its saved example response is illustrative.*

item.name: Courier
item.description: Carriers, pickup dates, pickup points and supported countries. `$client->courier()`.

item.name: available_carriers
item.description: Lists the carriers this account may ship with. Pass an entry's `servicecode` as `courier` in the other methods. `$client->courier()->getAvailableCarriers()`.

request.description: Without a payload every carrier enabled for the account is listed, with its code, name and whether it ships abroad.

response.name: Success: every carrier

request.description: `returncarrier` narrows the list to one carrier code.

With `additional_data: true`, each entry also has an `additional_data` object: cash on delivery (including whether it requires insurance), insurance, the services, shipment types and pickup rules the carrier supports, its points map and its own additional fields. `points_map` is null for a carrier without pickup points.

response.name: Success: with additional data

item.name: Success: with additional data, carrier with pickup points

request.description: `points_map` lists the point providers to show on the map and whether a sender or recipient point applies.

response.name: Success: with additional data, carrier with pickup points

request.description: An unknown code in `returncarrier` gives `[]`.

item.name: pickup_courier
item.description: Checks whether a carrier can collect on one day, and in which time windows. Nothing is booked: a collection is booked with the order (`create_order`'s `pickup`) or for several orders with `create_multi_order_pickup`. Without a date, today is checked. `$client->courier()->pickupCourier()`.

item.name: Success: date accepted, with time windows

request.description: `pickupdate: true` means the carrier can collect that day; `time` lists its windows.

response.name: Success: date accepted, with time windows

item.name: Success: date accepted, carrier without windows

request.description: Carriers without time windows return an empty `time` list with `pickupdate: true`.

response.name: Success: date accepted, carrier without windows

item.name: Error: carrier not available to the account

request.description: The message lists the accepted codes. No code fields.

response.name: Error: carrier not available to the account

request.description: Carriers that check the collection area need `shipfrom`.
The carrier's own message, with no code fields.
A weekend or public holiday is rejected.

item.name: get_courier_pickup_time
item.description: Lists the days a carrier can collect on, starting from today, with the windows available each day. `$client->courier()->getCourierPickupTime()`.

request.description: Days the carrier refuses are left out.
Carriers without time windows list the accepted days with an empty `time` list.

item.name: Error: carrier not available to the account

request.description: The message lists the accepted codes. No code fields.

item.name: get_countries
item.description: Lists the countries one international carrier delivers to. `$client->courier()->getCountries()`.

request.description: ISO country codes map to Polish names. A country with several names has them joined with ", " into one string.

request.description: The payload is `[]` rather than an object.

response.name: Success: carrier with no countries listed

request.description: Only international carriers are accepted. The message lists the accepted codes. No code fields.

item.name: get_supported_countries_v2
item.description: Lists every country the service supports, with its regions: the reference list for an address form. `$client->courier()->getSupportedCountries()`.

request.description: Each country has its ISO code, Polish name, EU membership, whether it is the default (Poland) and its regions. Region ids go in an address's province field. The list rarely changes.

item.name: get_courier_point
item.description: Finds pickup points across one or more carriers, or fetches one point by id. `$client->courier()->findCourierPoints()` (search) and `$client->courier()->getCourierPoint()` (by id).

request.description: The API returns `[]`, which `getCourierPoint()` reports as null.
At least one carrier is required, also with an `id`. The SDK checks this before sending.

item.name: Geo
item.description: Postcode lookups and the pickup point map token. `$client->geo()`.

item.name: find_city
item.description: Suggests localities for a Polish postcode, e.g. to autocomplete an address form. For `PL` the SDK checks the NN-NNN format before sending. `$client->geo()->findCity()`.

response.name: Success: several localities

request.description: A well-formed postcode that matches nothing returns `[]`.
Only Polish postcodes are supported; any other country returns `[]`.

item.name: get_map_token
item.description: Issues a short-lived token for the pickup point map widget. Unlike the API token, it is safe to expose in a browser. `$client->geo()->getMapToken()`.

request.description: Every call returns a new token. The map front-end authenticates with it directly.

item.name: Orders
item.description: Placing, pricing, tracking and cancelling orders. `$client->orders()`.

item.name: order_valuation_v2
item.description: Prices an order without placing it. Takes the same payload as `create_order`, which can still reject a payload that got a price. `$client->orders()->orderValuation()`.

request.description: Without `returnvaluations` the response lists one quote per carrier that can take the shipment, each with `serviceName` and the price split into net, gross, promotion and rebate parts.

item.name: create_order
item.description:
Places an order and returns a short receipt: the order number, waybills, price and tracking link. Every call books a separate shipment. `$client->orders()->createOrder()`.

**Changes data.** Running this folder creates, changes or deletes records on the account.

request.description: A one-parcel DPD shipment collected on the next working day. `label` lists the waybill numbers; the tracking link is for the first one.

item.name: Success: cash on delivery and insurance

request.description: The courier collects 250 PLN from the recipient and sends it to the bank account in `COD`. The parcel is insured for 500 PLN. The price includes both services.

response.name: Success: cash on delivery and insurance

request.description: Two identical boxes as one entry with `amount` 2, plus a non-standard parcel. Each parcel gets its own waybill, so `label` lists three numbers.

item.name: Success: parcel locker to parcel locker

request.description: `point_id` on the sender and the recipient names the lockers where the parcel is posted and collected. This service needs a pickup date but no time window.

response.name: Success: parcel locker to parcel locker

request.description: With the `LABELLESS` service and `nocourierorder` set, the sender posts the parcel at the locker without a printed label. The receipt adds `shipment_code`, the code shown at drop-off, which can be null.
A GLS shipment to Germany. GLS receipts add `consignid`, the carrier's consignment id, which can be null.

item.name: Success: cover address on the label

request.description: The `COVER_ADDRESS_SENDER` service prints `cover_address` on the label in place of the sender's address. `get_orders` returns it as the order's `cover_address`.

response.name: Success: cover address on the label

item.name: Success: with your own order ids

request.description: `external_application_id` and `external_order_id` link the order to your own record, so `get_orders` can find it by them, e.g. after a timeout. The SDK refuses one without the other.

response.name: Success: with your own order ids

To list orders, leave the key out; the SDK never sends it empty.

item.name: get_status
item.description: Current delivery status of one order, optionally with its scan history. `$client->orders()->getStatus()`.

request.description: The status name and code, when it was set (no seconds), the delivery date (no time; null until delivered) and the tracking link. `tracking` is empty.
`tracking: true` fills `tracking` with the carrier's scans: timestamp, status, location and description. It stays empty until the first scan, and asking for it makes the call slower.
No code fields.
`orderno` must look like `12345-678`. No code fields.
A cancelled order gets an error instead of a status; `get_orders` reads it. The number comes from `get_orders` / `Success: cancelled orders`.

item.name: get_label

request.description: A base64-encoded PDF in `file`.

*Manual request: skipped unless the `runManualRequests` variable is `true`. It needs data or codes you supply, or it changes things the collection can't put back. Its saved example response is illustrative.*

request.description: A DPD box from Poznań.
The same shipment with UPS gets `false`. `false` also comes back when the API can't evaluate the request, e.g. an incomplete one.

item.name: create_multi_order_pickup
item.description:
Books one courier collection for several orders placed with `multiPickup`. Orders succeed or fail one by one: `success` lists the booked numbers, `failed` maps each refused number to the reason. `$client->orders()->createMultiOrderPickup()`.

**Changes data.** Running this folder creates, changes or deletes records on the account.

request.description:

*Manual request: skipped unless the `runManualRequests` variable is `true`. It needs data or codes you supply, or it changes things the collection can't put back. Its saved example response is illustrative.*

item.name: Two-factor tokens
item.description: Two-factor confirmation for operations that need more than the API token: register a token, have the customer enter the code they received, verify it, then repeat the operation with the token and code. `$client->twoFactorToken()`.

item.description:
Starts a confirmation for one operation (`namespace`) and sends the customer a code. Only that operation accepts the token. `$client->twoFactorToken()->register()`.

**Changes data.** Running this folder creates, changes or deletes records on the account.

request.description:

item.name: save_contact_form

Submits a completed contact form. The answers go next to the category, form id and nonce from `get_contact_form`, keyed by the field names. `$client->tickets()->saveContactForm()`.

**Changes data.** Running this folder creates, changes or deletes records on the account.

request.description:
Submits the answers of a form fetched with `get_contact_form` for the same category. The response says what to show the customer next and, for a form that opens a ticket, its number. A form that needs the code sent by e-mail answers with `"status": "ERROR"`, `UPDATE_FORM` and a new `nonce`: show its auth code field and submit again.

*Manual request: skipped unless the `runManualRequests` variable is `true`. It needs data or codes you supply, or it changes things the collection can't put back. Its saved example response is illustrative.*

The invoice duplicate form refuses an invoice number the account doesn't have. A rejection has `"status": "ERROR"` in capitals, names each answer to fix in `validation_errors` and carries a fresh `nonce` for the next attempt.
The same nonce sent again after a submission. A nonce works once; fetch the form again, or use the fresh `nonce` from a rejection.
The category is unknown, has no form, or its form is website-only.
